name: Ahithophel
description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

points: After forty years Absalom asked leave to go pay his vow in Hebron, and the king said, Go in peace. But Absalom sent spies through all the tribes to say, at the sound of the trumpet, Absalom reigneth in Hebron. Two hundred men went with him from Jerusalem in their simplicity, knowing nothing. Absalom also sent for Ahithophel, David's counsellor, and the conspiracy was strong, for the people increased continually with Absalom.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: Ahithophel was such a good counsellor that his counsel was said to be like inquiring at the oracle of God, like talking to an angel of the Most High. So David prayed the Most High would turn that counsel into foolishness, and sent his friend Hushai to act like Absalom's servant so he could listen to Ahithophel's counsel and intervene. This was a game of chess, not checkers, and that is how we have to treat this thing today.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: Absalom asked Ahithophel for counsel, and Ahithophel said, Go in unto thy father's concubines whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father, and the hands of all with thee shall be strong. So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. The counsel of Ahithophel was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God.

Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Ahithophel had already given Absalom wicked counsel in the previous chapter, telling him to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel so that the hands of all that were with him would be made strong. Ahithophel was David's own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he set his house in order and hanged himself. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author; evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand
